note: Banks in Puerto Rico are numbered within the United States' routing number system: the ABA's Routing Number Policy says every one of the United States' territories falls into one of the twelve Federal Reserve districts, whose routing symbols the routing number begins with. The form is the United States' (a national form can't take another country's by prefix, which the engine reserves for an IBAN). The ABA's Routing Number Policy (read 2026-10-30 on aba.com; the policy's earlier revision was 2016) gives the routing number as nine digits: a four-digit Federal Reserve Routing Symbol (01-12 for banks, by Federal Reserve district), a four-digit ABA institution identifier (the page misprints it 'Intuition'), and a check digit. The form holds the routing number only, which identifies the bank (characters 1 to 8 before the check digit): no national standard read fixes the length of the account number itself, which each bank sets and which sits beside the routing number on a cheque. That length isn't modelled. The check digit's algorithm (the 3-7-1 weights) isn't stated on either ABA page read; the policy refers to the User Instructions of the ABA Key to Routing Numbers, which weren't read, so the weights aren't quoted here. NACHA's ACH developer guide (achdevguide.nacha.org) answered with a Cloudflare challenge and wasn't read.

sources.title: American Bankers Association, Routing Number Policy and Procedures (the Routing Number Administrative Board's policy, last revised before this copy in 2016)
sources.said: The Routing Number is a 9-digit number consisting of three components as shown below: XXXX YYYY C Federal Reserve Routing Symbol ABA Intuition Identifier Check Digit ... 01-12 Series: All checks and electronic transactions of banks ... One of the twelve geographic areas assigned to a Federal Reserve Bank main office. All of the United States and its territories fall into one of these twelve districts.
